quick: Ophthalmic 10% solution: 1-2 drops into the affected eye(s) every 2-3 hours initially
Topical use; avoid near term (theoretical kernicterus risk from sulfonamides)
Minimal systemic absorption from topical use; use with caution
No adjustment for topical use (negligible systemic absorption)
No relevant interaction with topical use
Clinical response; watch for local irritation or hypersensitivity
summary: Sulphacetamide (as the sodium salt) is a sulfonamide antibacterial used topically - most often as ophthalmic drops or ointment for superficial bacterial eye infections such as conjunctivitis and as adjunct therapy in trachoma, and in dermatological preparations for acne and seborrhoeic conditions. It is bacteriostatic, inhibiting bacterial folate synthesis. Although systemic absorption from topical use is low, sulfonamide hypersensitivity (including rare severe skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome) can occur, so it is avoided in patients with sulfonamide allergy.
indications: Treatment of conjunctivitis and other superficial ocular bacterial infections caused by susceptible organisms
Adjunctive treatment of trachoma (with systemic therapy)
Topical treatment of acne and seborrhoeic dermatitis (in dermatological combination products, e.g. with sulfur)

dosage.d: Instill 1-2 drops into the conjunctival sac(s) of the affected eye(s) every 2-3 hours initially
dosage.n: Taper by lengthening interval as the condition improves; usual course 7-10 days

dosage.d: Apply a small amount (about 1/2 inch) to the affected eye(s) up to four times daily and at bedtime
dosage.n: May combine daytime drops with bedtime ointment

dosage.d: Instill 2 drops into the affected eye(s) every 2 hours
dosage.n: Must be accompanied by systemic therapy

dosage.d: Apply a thin film to affected skin once or twice daily

admin: Wash hands before use; tilt the head back and instill drops into the conjunctival sac without touching the dropper to the eye or lashes
Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner (punctal occlusion) for a minute after drops to reduce systemic absorption
For ointment, pull down the lower lid and apply a thin ribbon inside
Do not use while wearing soft contact lenses; remove lenses and wait before reinserting
Discard the solution if it becomes discoloured (darkened) or after the recommended in-use period
moa: Sulphacetamide is a sulfonamide that competitively inhibits bacterial dihydropteroate synthase, blocking the incorporation of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) into folic acid. This impairs bacterial synthesis of folate and ultimately nucleic acids, producing a bacteriostatic effect against susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to sulfonamides or any component
Infants under 2 months (for some systemic-risk formulations)
relative: History of severe sulfonamide reactions (e.g. SJS/TEN)
Use with caution in the presence of significant local irritation
monitor: Signs of secondary or non-susceptible (e.g. fungal) overgrowth with prolonged use

preg: Topical/ophthalmic use gives low systemic exposure and is generally considered acceptable when needed. As a sulfonamide, avoid significant exposure near term because systemic sulfonamides can displace bilirubin and theoretically increase neonatal kernicterus risk.
lact: Systemic absorption from topical ophthalmic use is minimal, so meaningful transfer to milk is unlikely. Use with caution; systemic sulfonamides are generally avoided in mothers nursing ill, premature or jaundiced infants.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for topical or ophthalmic use because systemic absorption is negligible.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for topical or ophthalmic use.

major: Silver-containing ophthalmic preparations e.g. silver nitrate (chemically incompatible - do not use together)
moderate: Para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and PABA-containing local anaesthetics e.g. procaine, tetracaine (antagonise the antibacterial effect)
Gentamicin and certain other topical agents (possible antagonism in some combinations)
minor: Other topical ophthalmic medicines (separate instillation by several minutes)
interactions.alcohol: No relevant interaction with topical use
interactions.diagnostics: Negligible systemic effect; no significant interference with laboratory tests at topical doses

common: Transient local stinging or burning on instillation
serious: Hypersensitivity reactions including local oedema and conjunctival reaction
Stevens-Johnson syndrome and other severe cutaneous sulfonamide reactions (rare, can be fatal)
Superinfection with non-susceptible organisms on prolonged use
rare: Fatal sulfonamide reactions (e.g. agranulocytosis, hepatic necrosis) - reported with systemic sulfonamides
emergency: Signs of Stevens-Johnson syndrome (skin blistering, mucosal involvement, fever)

monitoring: Clinical resolution of the eye/skin infection
Watch for non-resolving infection or overgrowth of resistant/fungal organisms with prolonged use
counsel: Wash your hands before and after using the eye drops or ointment
Do not let the dropper or tube tip touch your eye, lashes or any surface
Vision may blur briefly after use - wait before driving
Do not wear soft contact lenses during treatment
Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, or if redness, swelling or a rash develops, and stop using it
pk: Local antibacterial action begins promptly after application
High local tissue concentrations at the application site
Systemic half-life of absorbed sulfacetamide ~7-13 hours; negligible absorption with topical use
Brief local effect - requires frequent instillation initially
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light; discard if the solution darkens
pearls: Avoid in patients with a sulfonamide (sulfa) allergy - cross-reactivity and rare severe skin reactions can occur even with topical use
PABA and PABA-derived local anaesthetics antagonise its action; silver-containing preparations are incompatible
Discard solution that has darkened - discoloration indicates degradation
Frequent initial dosing then tapering as the infection responds is the typical ophthalmic regimen
Combination dermatological products pair sulfacetamide with sulfur for acne and seborrhoeic dermatitis
missed: For eye drops or ointment used at intervals, apply the missed dose as soon as you remember, then continue the usual schedule. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Complete the full course even if the eye looks better.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity; excess drops simply overflow. Accidental ingestion of ophthalmic solution rarely causes significant effects but, with large sulfonamide exposure, could theoretically cause nausea, gastrointestinal upset and (with systemic sulfonamides) crystalluria or blood dyscrasias. Manage supportively and seek advice for substantial ingestion.
